# Project word list — soroauth spell check (issue #151)
#
# One lowercase token per line. Tokens are what the checker's tokenizer can
# produce: runs of ASCII letters, case-folded, split at lower→upper
# boundaries. An entry with digits, punctuation or uppercase can never be
# seen by the checker and is rejected by New (fail closed), which is why
# every line here is a plain lowercase word.
#
# This file is NOT a whitelist consulted per token: the checker only flags
# a token when it is on the misspelling list or is a doubled English
# function word ("the the"). An unlisted word is never a finding, which is
# why protocol terms can never fail the check. Each row records why the
# term exists so the next maintainer can tell a real word from an accident.
#
# Adding a row here means adding the same reason to its comment.

# --- Project and package names ---
# soroauth: this library and CLI (github.com/soroauth/soroauth-go).
soroauth
# go-stellar-sdk tokenizes as "go" + "stellar" + "sdk", all ordinary words
# or covered below; "stellar" is here because it also appears inside
# identifiers like "stellarExpert" and "stellarcli".
stellar
# stellar-cli, stellar-core, stellar.expert: the token "cli" also appears
# in prose ("the CLI"); "expert" appears in stellar.expert explorer links.
cli
expert

# --- Stellar protocol and ecosystem terms ---
# Soroban: the smart contracts platform (soroban.sdf.org). Tokenizes from
# "Soroban", "soroban-", "soroban_testnet", "SorobanAuthorizationEntry" and
# every camelCase variant.
soroban
# strkey / strkeys: the Stellar string encoding of keys (G…/C…/M…
# addresses); the plural is one letters run.
strkey
# xdr: External Data Representation, the wire encoding (RFC 4506), from
# "XDR" in prose; an all-caps acronym stays one letters run.
xdr
# scval / scaddress / screference and the other Sc-prefixed SDK type names
# in prose: they tokenize to the lowercase forms below.
scval
scaddress
# muxed: muxed accounts (CAP-45 style M… addresses).
muxed
# fee bump: a fee-bump transaction's inner transaction (CAP-15).
fee

# --- Signing and crypto terms ---
# ed: the letters run left when digits split "ed25519" / "Ed25519Signer".
ed
# sha: SHA-256 hash (the letters run of "sha256" and "SHA-256").
sha
# hmac: HMAC-SHA-256 constructions in the SAC and token narratives.
hmac

# --- CAP and envelope names in prose ---
# The token "cap" (from "CAP-46-11", "CAP-71-01") is an ordinary word; the
# numbers are invisible to the tokenizer, no row is needed for the numbers.
# envelope: TransactionEnvelope, fee-bump envelope prose.
envelope
# invokehost: the camelCase split half of "invokeHostFunction" (the other
# half, "function", is ordinary English).
invokehost
# authorizationentry: camelCase splits "AuthorizationEntry" into
# "authorization" + "entry", both ordinary; this row covers prose that
# writes the name without the boundary.

# --- Testing and CI vocabulary ---
# testnet: Stellar's public test network, named throughout.
testnet
# e2e: the build tag and directory. "e" is a single letter (never checked);
# the digit "2" is invisible. "e2e" as a whole can never be a token, so no
# row exists for it: this comment is the record.
# friendbot: the testnet faucet.
friendbot
# codecov: the coverage service the CI workflow publishes to.
codecov
# gofmt / govulncheck style go-tool names in prose: "gofmt" tokenizes as
# "gofmt"; "govet" as "govet"; the vet and fmt binaries are standard tools.
gofmt
# xeon: the Intel CPU model named in measured-commit evidence bodies.
xeon

# --- Domain prose that is not standard English but is intended ---
# strkeys: plural of strkey; the letters run is "strkeys" as a whole.
strkeys
# signers, per the README's signer table prose; ordinary English, listed
# because "signer" appears in identifier contexts like "ed25519Signer".
signer
